fluff.overview: The Estevez was an eighty-ton tracked main battle tank produced by Novais Motors on New Avalon, named for a popular local militia officer. Introduced in 2310, it was one of the earliest effective armored fighting vehicles developed outside the Terran Hegemony. The design predated the formal founding of the Federated Suns by several years, serving the disparate political entities on New Avalon that would eventually coalesce into the young nation. Its combination of thick armor, substantial firepower, and imposing physical presence made the Estevez the dominant main battle tank in the region throughout the twenty-fourth century. The vehicle's sheer size and power earned it a fearsome reputation among its contemporaries, as lighter armed opponents often chose to retreat rather than engage the massive tank head-on.
fluff.capabilities:
Powered by the NM/750 Combat Diesel engine, the Estevez could reach a maximum speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour, competitive with many lighter tanks of its era despite the vehicle's eighty-ton mass. The tank's primary armament consisted of a turret-mounted Avalon Slugger Heavy Rifle, a large-caliber weapon that delivered punishing hits against contemporary targets. Seven tons of stored ammunition gave the Estevez exceptional battlefield endurance, though this massive magazine also represented a significant vulnerability, as a single penetrating hit risked detonating the entire stockpile. Two coaxial PC-50 machine guns and a pair of vehicular grenade launchers provided secondary defense against infantry threats.

Ten and a half tons of Nova-IV Hyper-Composite with Diamond Flex armor gave the Estevez robust protection for its time, rated at BAR 8 across all facings. The Valiant Echo Mk. II communications system and Thermoscan Optics fire control system were adequate for the early twenty-fourth century but grew increasingly outmatched as military technology advanced. The vehicle required a crew of nine, including two officers, two enlisted crew, and five gunners, a substantial manpower requirement that complicated logistics. The design's fuel-thirsty diesel engine further strained supply lines, limiting operational range relative to more efficient contemporaries.
fluff.deployment: The standard Estevez served as the primary main battle tank of the Federated Suns throughout the twenty-fourth century. Typically deployed along border regions and in garrison postings, the base model was optimized for direct engagement of enemy armored vehicles and fixed fortifications. Its deep ammunition reserves suited it to sustained operations far from established supply lines, and the vehicle's imposing profile alone was often sufficient to deter lightly armed opponents from pressing an engagement.
fluff.history:
The Estevez entered service in 2310 and quickly became the backbone of armored forces across the nascent Federated Suns. During the sporadic border conflicts of the pre-Age of War period, the tank exemplified what contemporaries called "tank shock." Its imposing bulk and massive main cannon caused many opposing forces to break formation and retreat rather than stand against it. Some military historians later argued that the Federated Suns was built upon the Estevez rather than upon the ideals of the "Six Liberties," evidence of the vehicle's outsized role in securing the young nation's borders. The Free Worlds League recognized the design's effectiveness and produced a licensed copy designated the Kestrel MBT, which was identical in combat capability.

By the early 2400s, advancing military technology had rendered the Estevez obsolete. Its main weapon proved increasingly ineffective against modern armor compositions, and the inability to fire specialized munitions left it at a growing tactical disadvantage. The vehicle's substantial logistical demands further strained the resources of the Federated Peacekeeping Forces, while opponents discovered that targeting the tracks could disable and bypass even an otherwise intact tank.

The Estevez's only encounter with BattleMechs occurred during a Draconis Combine deep raid on Robinson. The Kuritan commander, a firm believer in the Ares Conventions, proposed the engagement be conducted with simulated munitions. The Combine 'Mechs overwhelmed the Estevez MBTs with ease and achieved their objective without difficulty. Subsequent analysis determined that even with live ammunition, a full regiment of tanks could not have defeated the Kuritan heavy 'Mech battalion. The demonstration confirmed what many military planners already suspected: conventional armor of the Estevez's generation was hopelessly outclassed by BattleMech technology.

Following its withdrawal from frontline service, a number of Estevez hulls received new turrets mounting lighter autocannon for use as anti-aircraft platforms. This conversion provided a modest extension of service life in the garrison role, but the aging chassis could not be economically maintained alongside newer equipment. By the mid-twenty-fifth century, the Federated Suns had retired the Estevez entirely in favor of the Tiger medium tank, and all remaining vehicles were scrapped.
